keys.statement: Reactive distillation is feasible only where the temperature and pressure windows of the reaction, the catalyst and the separation overlap. Otherwise keep reactor and column separate, and judge integration on the whole process.

source.locator: Heuristic approaches, journal p. 1268 (p. 7 of the TU Delft copy)

decisions.obstacle: Reaction and separation may need different conditions.
decisions.mechanism: One column imposes one pressure and a temperature profile.
decisions.operation: Check the overlap before choosing reactive distillation.

keys.statement: A slow reaction makes reactive distillation unattractive, and a very high relative volatility needs only a reactor followed by a flash. Between these, reactive distillation is a candidate.

source.locator: Heuristic approaches, journal pp. 1268-1269 (pp. 7-8 of the TU Delft copy, Fig. 2)

decisions.obstacle: Choosing between reactor plus separator and a reactive column.
decisions.mechanism: Rate and volatility decide whether stages help.
decisions.operation: Place the system on a rate-volatility chart.
limits: The chart's axes are not quantified; the authors warn that it needs experience to use.

keys.statement: If the reaction is too slow at the column's temperatures, raising the column pressure raises the temperature and thus the rate, as long as separation and catalyst still allow it.

decisions.expected_change: Faster reaction in the reactive zone.

keys.statement: Put the reactive zone where reactant concentrations are highest. Estimate the non-reactive stages with Fenske-type shortcuts and the reactive stages from the reactive height over the catalytic packing's HETP.

decisions.mechanism: Conventional shortcuts give the separating sections.
decisions.operation: Shortcut sizing of the reactive and separating sections.

keys.statement: For reactions with a large heat effect, integrate energy between the reactive and separating sections; for slow, strongly endothermic reactions with small equilibrium constants also integrate mass with the stripping section. For thermally neutral reactions mass integration alone suffices.

source.locator: Synthesis procedures, journal p. 1277 (p. 16 of the TU Delft copy; procedure of Huang et al.)

decisions.obstacle: Reaction heat disturbs the column's vapour and liquid flows.
decisions.mechanism: Heat released or absorbed on the reactive stages changes the internal flows.
decisions.operation: Plan internal energy or mass integration according to the heat effect.
